correctness.rationale: At each coordinate, the three binary disagreement indicators sum to either zero or two, proving the universal \(\lfloor2n/3\rfloor\) upper bound. Stable extension on a bidirected path is equivalent to independent domination. The finite witnesses at sizes \(4,5,7,8,9\) achieve the bound, and an explicit three-column insertion preserves stable semantics and raises all three pairwise distances by two; those bases cover every \(n\ge7\). The five independent dominating sets of \(P_6\) have a threshold-four distance graph equal to a five-cycle, giving an optimum of three. The standalone checker exhaustively verifies \(4\le n\le20\) and constructive witnesses through \(n=600\); the unbounded claim follows from the proof, not from finite replay.

value.rationale: The exact three-viewpoint packing radius is the natural next invariant after published pairwise extension diversity: simultaneous robustness requires all three alternatives to be mutually separated, unlike merely maximizing one pair. A complete sharp classification on bidirected paths provides all orders, a universal upper bound, structural attainment construction, and a genuine exceptional order six. This precise natural invariant describes how many mutually different stable alternatives a linear attack structure can support.
